config.title: Creating RTK Endpoints (from zero)

intro.title: Creating RTK Endpoints — React + TypeScript
intro.body: You will build a working data layer from scratch — no prior Redux Toolkit, RTK Query, React, or TypeScript experience assumed. Step by step you will: connect fetchBaseQuery to the free JSONPlaceholder API, write TypeScript interfaces that lock in your response shapes, register query endpoints for a post list and a single post, add a mutation endpoint that POSTs to the API and invalidates the cache, wire it all into a Redux store, wrap the app with Provider, and drive three real UI states — loading, error, and success — entirely from hook return values. You leave with a working mental model you can operate: createApi → typed endpoints → auto-generated hooks → UI.
intro.usecase: Every production app — ecommerce catalog, analytics dashboard, social feed — needs the same four things RTK Query handles for you: typed HTTP calls, automatic caching, cache invalidation after writes, and predictable loading UX. JSONPlaceholder gives you a live API to practice against without keys, billing, or backend setup, so every pattern you apply here transfers directly to real backends on day one.

objectives: Create an empty API slice using createApi with fetchBaseQuery typed to a base URL and an empty endpoints object so the design pattern is reusable, and async data is handled with an explicit and safe data shape.
Inject a typed query endpoint into an existing API slice using the injectEndpoints method so the learner can explain both the mechanism and the visible result.
Establish the endpoint's query function typed as (arg: ArgType) => string | FetchArgs to build the request URL so the contract is explicit and incorrect usage is caught early.
Export the injected endpoint's auto-generated typed hook and consume it in a feature component so the learner can explain both the mechanism and the visible result.

steps.title: Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery in api.ts
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, import `createApi` and `fetchBaseQuery` from `'@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'`. These two functions are the foundation of RTK Query in React.
steps.hint: Exact path: `@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react` (includes React hooks integration).

steps.title: Define the Post interface
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, export an `interface Post` with `id: number`, `userId: number`, `title: string`, and `body: string`. This matches a typical `/posts` object from JSONPlaceholder.
steps.hint: Field names and types must match what the API returns so TypeScript can trust your data.
steps.analogousExample: export interface Post { id: number; userId: number; title: string; body: string }

steps.title: Create the API with createApi
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, export a `const` assigned to `createApi({})` (empty object for now). Use any clear name you like — canonical seeds use `jsonPlaceholderApi`. Next steps add `reducerPath`, `baseQuery`, and `endpoints`.
steps.hint: Example: `export const postsApi = createApi({ });` — the important part is calling and exporting `createApi`.

steps.feedbackWrong: Call createApi with an empty object and export the API instance from api.ts.

steps.title: Set reducerPath
steps.instruction: Inside `createApi`, add `reducerPath: '…'` using a **string literal** of your choice (often the same text as your API const so the Redux state key is easy to spot). It must be unique in the store.
steps.hint: Example: `reducerPath: 'postsApi'` if your const is `postsApi`.

steps.feedbackWrong: Add reducerPath with a string literal inside createApi in api.ts.

steps.title: Add baseQuery with JSONPlaceholder baseUrl
steps.instruction: Add `baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com' })` inside `createApi`. Every relative path in your endpoints will be appended to this base URL.
steps.hint: JSONPlaceholder is free and requires no API key — ideal for learning.

steps.title: Add an empty endpoints builder
steps.instruction: Add `endpoints: (builder) => ({})` to `createApi`. The `builder` object is how you register **query** (read) and **mutation** (write) endpoints.
steps.hint: Returning `{}` is valid — you will add keys like `getPosts` next.

steps.title: Add getPosts query (shape only)
steps.instruction: Inside the endpoints object, add `getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' })`. This says: “GET /posts relative to baseUrl”. Skip TypeScript generics for one step so the shape is clear.
steps.hint: The hook name will be `useGetPostsQuery` — derived from `getPosts`.

steps.title: Type getPosts as Post[]
steps.instruction: Change the call to `builder.query<Post[], void>({ ... })` so TypeScript knows the response is an array of `Post` and the hook takes no argument (`void`).
steps.hint: Post[] = many posts; void = useGetPostsQuery() with no id parameter.

steps.title: Add getPost query (single post by id)
steps.instruction: Add `getPost: builder.query<Post, number>({ query: (postId) => `/posts/${postId}` })` so one post can be loaded by numeric id. JSONPlaceholder supports `GET /posts/:id`.
steps.hint: The second generic is the argument type — here a number id.

steps.title: Declare tagTypes for cache invalidation
steps.instruction: At the top level of `createApi` (next to `reducerPath`), add `tagTypes: ['Post']`. Tags are labels RTK Query uses to know which cached data to refresh after a mutation.
steps.hint: We use one tag string `'Post'` for all post-related data in this lesson.

steps.title: Add providesTags to list and detail queries
steps.instruction: On both `getPosts` and `getPost` endpoint configs, add `providesTags: ['Post']` (same array on each). That marks cached results as belonging to the `Post` tag family.
steps.hint: When a mutation invalidates `Post`, both list and detail can refetch.

steps.title: Add NewPost type and addPost mutation
steps.instruction: Export `type NewPost = Pick<Post, 'title' | 'body' | 'userId'>`. Add `addPost: builder.mutation<Post, NewPost>({ query: (body) => ({ url: '/posts', method: 'POST', body, headers: { 'Content-type': 'application/json; charset=UTF-8' } }), invalidatesTags: ['Post'] })`. JSONPlaceholder accepts POST and returns a fake created post.
steps.hint: mutation = changing server data; invalidatesTags refreshes list data after add.

steps.title: Export generated hooks
steps.instruction: After `createApi`, export hooks: `export const { useGetPostsQuery, useGetPostQuery, useAddPostMutation } = <yourApiConst>;` — use the **same** const you exported for your API. Hook names are auto-generated from your endpoint keys.
steps.hint: Hook prefix is `use`, suffix is `Query` or `Mutation`.
steps.analogousExample: export const { useGetPostsQuery, useGetPostQuery, useAddPostMutation } = jsonPlaceholderApi;

steps.title: Import configureStore in store.ts
steps.instruction: In **store.ts**, add `import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';` and import **your** API instance from `'./api'` using the name you exported in api.ts (e.g. `import { postsApi } from './api';`).
steps.hint: The store must see the same symbol you exported from api.ts.
steps.analogousExample:
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import { jsonPlaceholderApi } from './api';

seedCode.App.tsx:

// Next: the API slice will live in api.ts

steps.expectedOutcome: store.ts imports configureStore and the API module.
steps.feedbackPartial: Import configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and your API from './api'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add configureStore and an import from ./api at the top of store.ts.

steps.title: Create the store with reducer and middleware
steps.instruction: Export `store` from **store.ts** with `configureStore`: put your API’s reducer under `[yourApi.reducerPath]` and `.concat(yourApi.middleware)` on the default middleware. Use the **same** API const you imported from `./api`.
steps.hint: Never forget `.concat(api.middleware)` — without it, RTK Query cannot run requests.

steps.feedbackWrong: Use configureStore with your API reducer and middleware.

steps.title: Wrap UI with Provider in App.tsx
steps.instruction: In **App.tsx**, import `Provider` from `'react-redux'`, import `store` from `'./store'`, and export a default `Root` component that renders `<Provider store={store}><App /></Provider>`. Keep a simple `App` inner component that returns a heading for now.
steps.hint: Provider makes the Redux store available to hooks like `useGetPostsQuery`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The tree is wrapped with Provider.
steps.feedbackPartial: Import Provider and store; wrap your app JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use Provider with store={store} around App.

steps.title: Call useGetPostsQuery inside App
steps.instruction: Inside the inner `App` component, import `useGetPostsQuery` from `'./api'`, call it, and destructure `data`, `isLoading`, `error`, and `refetch`.
steps.hint: Hooks that use RTK Query must run inside a component under Provider.
steps.analogousExample: const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = useGetPostsQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: List query hook runs in the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: Destructure data, isLoading, error, refetch from useGetPostsQuery().
steps.feedbackWrong: Call useGetPostsQuery in App and destructure the result.

steps.title: Show loading state
steps.instruction:
While `isLoading` is true, render a short message such as `

Loading…

`.
steps.hint:
Conditional render: `{isLoading &&

Loading…

}`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Users see feedback while the request runs.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use isLoading in JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: Conditionally render a loading message when isLoading is true.

steps.title: Show error state
steps.instruction: If `error` is truthy, render a simple error message. RTK Query sets `error` when the HTTP request fails.
steps.hint: Keep the message user-friendly — no need to dump the whole object.
steps.expectedOutcome: Failures are visible in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: Render a paragraph when error is set.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add conditional rendering for error in App.

steps.title: Render the post titles in a list
steps.instruction:
Map `data` to an unordered list: each `post` gets `
  • {post.title}
    • `. Use optional chaining on `data` if you like (`data?.map`).
steps.hint: Always set `key` to a stable id from the server.
steps.expectedOutcome: Titles appear from the API response.
steps.feedbackPartial: Map over data and show post.title with key post.id.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use data.map (or data?.map) to render list items.

steps.title: Add a Refetch button
steps.instruction: Destructure already includes `refetch`. Add `<button type="button" onClick={() => refetch()}>Refetch</button>` to manually reload posts (helps you see caching vs network).
steps.hint: refetch() returns a promise you can await in advanced cases.
steps.expectedOutcome: User can trigger a reload.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add a button that calls refetch.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use onClick with refetch from useGetPostsQuery.

steps.title: Track selected post id with useState
steps.instruction: Import `useState` from React. Add `const [postId, setPostId] = useState<number | null>(null);` inside `App`. You will pass `postId` into the detail query next.
steps.hint: null means “no post selected yet”.
steps.expectedOutcome: Component can remember which post is selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add useState for postId typed number | null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare postId state in App.

steps.title: Call useGetPostQuery with skip
steps.instruction: Import `useGetPostQuery`. Call `useGetPostQuery(postId!, { skip: postId == null })` so no request runs until a post is selected. Destructure `data` as `onePost` to avoid clashing with the list `data`.
steps.hint: skip prevents calling `/posts/undefined`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Detail query runs only when postId is set.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use skip: postId == null with useGetPostQuery.
steps.feedbackWrong: Call useGetPostQuery with skip when postId is null.

steps.title: Select a post from the list
steps.instruction: Next to each title, add a button `View #id` that calls `setPostId(post.id)`.
steps.hint: This updates state and triggers the detail query.
steps.expectedOutcome: User can open one post.
steps.feedbackPartial: Wire onClick to setPostId with the post's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add buttons that set postId from each list item.

steps.title: Render the selected post body
steps.instruction: When `onePost` exists, render a `<section>` with the post id as a heading and `onePost.body` in a paragraph.
steps.hint: Optional: add a “Clear” button that sets postId back to null.
steps.expectedOutcome: Detail text shows under the list.
steps.feedbackPartial: Show onePost.body when onePost is defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: Conditionally render section with onePost.body.

steps.title: Import useAddPostMutation
steps.instruction: Import `useAddPostMutation` from `'./api'` and call it in `App`: `const [addPost, { isLoading: adding }] = useAddPostMutation();`.
steps.hint: Tuple pattern: first item is trigger function, second is meta (loading, error…).
steps.expectedOutcome: Mutation hook is available.
steps.feedbackPartial: Destructure the mutation trigger from useAddPostMutation.
steps.feedbackWrong: Call useAddPostMutation inside App.

steps.title: Controlled inputs for new post
steps.instruction: Add `title` and `body` string state with two `<input>` elements (controlled: `value` + `onChange`).
steps.hint: JSONPlaceholder expects title, body, and userId for new posts.
steps.expectedOutcome: User can type a fake new post.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use useState for title and body and wire inputs.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add controlled inputs for title and body.

steps.title: Submit addPost with demo userId
steps.instruction: On a button click, call `addPost({ title, body, userId: 1 })`, then clear the fields. Disable the button while `adding` is true.
steps.hint: userId 1 is a safe demo choice on JSONPlaceholder.
steps.expectedOutcome: Mutation runs against the free API.
steps.feedbackPartial: Call addPost with an object and handle loading state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Wire button to addPost with title, body, userId.

steps.title: Understand what you built
steps.instruction: Confirm your **api.ts** defines: typed queries (`getPosts`, `getPost`), a typed mutation (`addPost`), tags, and exported hooks. Confirm **store.ts** registers reducer + middleware. Confirm **App.tsx** uses hooks under `Provider`. No code change required — click CHECK if your files still contain these pieces.
steps.hint: RTK Query = endpoints + generated hooks + cache. JSONPlaceholder = reproducible practice data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You can explain the three-file split.
successCriteria: You reviewed api.ts, store.ts, and App.tsx.
steps.feedbackCorrect: ✅ Nice recap — one polish step left.
steps.feedbackPartial: Scroll through all three files and match them to the checklist.
steps.feedbackWrong: Ensure exports and Provider are still present.

steps.title: Export default Root
steps.instruction: Ensure **App.tsx** default export is the `Root` component (or equivalent) that wraps `App` with `Provider` and `store`. This is the entry pattern for Vite/React.
steps.hint: `export default function Root`
steps.expectedOutcome: Default export wraps Provider correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: Default export should be the component that renders Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: Export Root as default with Provider and store.
